newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA ENJOYING TOP SPOT -- WHILE IT LASTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA ENJOYING TOP SPOT -- WHILE IT LASTS.

text.p: Vicenza coach Francesco Guidolin is doing his best to play down the historic achievment of his provincial side who went top of Italy's Serie A for or the first time in their 94-year history following a 2-0 home win against Reggiana on Sunday.
Having won that game in the afternoon, Vicenza then had to await the outcome of the evening's Milan derby between league leaders Internazionale and champions AC Milan.

If Inter had won they would have regained top spot, but a 1-1 draw in the Milan derby guaranteed Vicenza's position -- a point clear of promoted Bologna -- who have also astounded the critics by starting so well -- and Inter, who slipped to third.
But with 10 matches played, Guidolin is almost more happy that his Vicenza side have picked up enough points to ensure their survival in Serie A than he is thinking in terms of winning the title.
"The important thing today is not that we are top of the table but that we have picked up 20 points, half of what we require to ensure first division survival
"I don't want to denegrate my side's achievement but I'm a realist and I know that the really strong sides in this championship have yet to play to their best"

For most of the last 20 years, Vicenza has been a second and third division side, best known for having launched the careers of two Italian World Cup heroes -- Paolo Rossi who played in 1992 and Roberto Baggio who played in 1990 and 1994.
A thriving industrial centre set in a rich agricultural zone approximately halfway between Venice and Verona, the town of Vicenza has boosted a competitive soccer team since 1902.
The arrival of coach Guidolin in the 1994-95 season prompted a major revival with the team winning promotion to Serie A, encouraging the club to build its player resources.

For its return to Serie A, Vicenza bought a host of experienced but little known players such as the Uruguyans Marcel Otero of Penarol and Gustavo Mendez of Nacional Montevideo as well as Giampiero Maini of AS Roma, Roberto Murgita of Genoa, Davide Belotti of Nola, Luca Mondini of Inter, Gabriele Ambrosetti of Brescia and Daniele Amerini of Fiorentina.
The new team blended immediately to have an excellent season, finising ninth on 49 points and just outside the UEFA qualifying zone.
The side has maintained that level of performance this season, having already beaten more fancied opponents such as Juventus at home and Fiorentina and Lazio away.
One interested observer of the Vicenza success story has been former club star Paolo Rossi, a protagonist in the club's previous best ever year.
The 21-year-old Rossi scored 24 goals for Vicenza in the 1977-78 season to end up the league's leading goalscorer and inspiring Vicenza to a second place finish, five points behind Juventus.
Rossi, who now lives in Vicenza where he runs a real estate agency, regularily attends home games :
"The current Vicenza is a good team. I see them often and all the best teams have problems when they come here.
"If you think that my Vicenza side didn't make nearly as good a start back in '77 as this one, then I'd say that they'll have a good season", Rossi said on Italian radio on Monday.
Coach Guidolin, however, does not intend to sit around on his new found laurels and is already preparing to pull off another major shock.
On Wednesday, Vicenza go into a second leg Italian Cup quarter final tie at home to Milan after having drawn the first leg 1-1 in Milan two weeks ago.

"Being top of the league is a bonus for my boys, for their spirit of sacrifice. This is an extraordinary moment for the fans and the club but, for us, we're already preparing for Wednesday's Cup tie against Milan".
